items.rootCause: Reanimated 4.5.1 on Android keeps the last props of every view an animated style wrote in the last ~2 s in AnimatedPropsRegistry. That includes a write on mount: ViewDescriptorsSet.add calls updater(true), so every card's press and every Enter is in the registry for its first ~2 s. performNonLayoutOperations re-applies the whole registry (getPendingUpdates returns every tag) on every UI-thread event, including each first draw of a react-native-svg shape (VirtualView.setClientRect). A deleted view still in the registry fails each time, with a full stack trace, about 1 ms per failure. Opening History: 24 skeleton blocks pulsing on a worklet were deleted against ~370 new card shapes, about 8,900 failures (fixed in the first round with CSS loaders). The reviewer's medium issue was confirmed in code and fixed this round. The same freeze came back whenever one list replaced another in a single commit. History filter switch: once both sources are loaded, loader.show resolves in microtasks, so the old cards (PressableCard and Enter, ~20-40 registered views) could be deleted in the frame that draws the new cards' avatars. History 'נסה שוב': the failure StateView, with its just-pressed button, was replaced by cards in one commit. Leaderboard tab or table size: setTab plus setSnap(feed.peek) brought a cached board's rows and podium in the same commit that deleted the old ones. Estimated at thousands of failures (seconds) for a tab switch and back within ~2 s.
items.fix: First round (kept): Skeleton and Spinner loops are Reanimated CSS animations (cssMotion.ts, SKELETON_PULSE, SPINNER_TURN). CSS animations are not in AnimatedPropsRegistry, so every skeleton-to-content swap is safe (History, leaderboard, player card, progress/achievements, Home recent games, blocked list). This round: retire.ts adds SWAP_FRAMES = 2 and framesPassed(n). HistoryScreen.pick shows the skeleton at once and resolves the new page with Promise.all([loader.show(next), framesPassed(2)]). HistoryScreen.run takes swapFrom. When the answer turns cards into a state or a state into cards (hasCards differs), it commits setSnap(null) (the skeleton) first and the answer afterFrames(2) later. reload passes the shown page, so retry from the failure state goes failure → skeleton → cards. A retry that fails again keeps the same StateView. LeaderboardScreen.show: when the tab or size changes, a `swapping` state (keyed by request id) makes the table (rows and podium) show its loading skeleton for at least 2 frames. The answer is joined with the same gap. The rest of the screen (tabs, caption, pinned 'me' row from the cached board) updates at once, so the pinned row never blinks. The same tab again (retry) keeps its rows as before. more() is ignored while swapping. No UI strings changed.

(2) Offline, then retry with the network back: the StateView is gone and the skeleton shows; cards only after 2 frames. (3) A retry that fails again keeps the same StateView instance. New leaderboardSwap.test.tsx: going back to a cached tab shows no rows and no podium, the loading skeleton, and the new caption, selected tab and pinned row at once; rows and podium appear only after frame 2. Same check for the 2/3 size picker. (1), (2) and both leaderboard tests fail on the old code, where rows and cards appeared right after the microtasks. The settle helpers in LeaderboardScreen, LeaderboardStates, HistoryScreen and HistoryStates now wait for timers, because a frame is setTimeout(0) under Jest. The skeleton pulses and the cards replace it in under 1 s. No frame over ~200 ms (was 6,494-6,928 ms). 0 failures (was 6,700-8,900). Same for 'טבלת מובילים' and 'הישגים'. items.rootCause: The 2 failing tags are the in-app back button's TactileSurface body and face. The press moves them with worklet styles, and the screen is popped (its views deleted) ~150-300 ms later, well inside Reanimated's ~2 s hold. Refined this round, from code (reviewer issue 6): the ~30 updates per tag over ~150 ms are most likely not new Home SVG shapes. homeTransitions.test.tsx shows Home does not re-render on return, so React creates no new shapes on Home. Any event dispatched on the UI thread triggers the re-apply (NodesManager.onEventDispatch → handleEvent + performOperations). react-native-screens dispatches a ScreenTransitionProgressEvent on every animation frame of the pop, for each moving screen (ScreensAnimation.applyTransformation → ScreenFragment.dispatchTransitionProgressEvent). That is about 2 events per frame, ~27 in 150 ms at 90 Hz, which matches ~30 per tag. System Back fires the same events, but no stale tags are in the registry, hence 0. So removing Home redraws would not help. Not verified on the device: one logged stack trace would confirm it (ScreenFragment.dispatchTransitionProgressEvent instead of VirtualView.setClientRect).
items.fix: No code change, still Moshe's decision. Option (1): the native patch to Reanimated NodesManager.onEventDispatch, so a UI-thread event skips handleEvent/performOperations when isAnyHandlerWaitingForEvent is false. It also covers the transition events and every other remaining case. Option (2): drive the TactileSurface press with Reanimated CSS transitions. That changes the press feel and latency of every button. docs/PERF.md (B14/B32, 'הרצת QA 3') now holds the refined analysis and the wider class this belongs to. Any screen deleted within ~2.5 s of mounting or of a press fails on each transition event: back from History right after the cards appear, and tab-to-tab replace (History ↔ Leaderboard ↔ Achievements), estimated at seconds. For tab-to-tab a JS alternative is listed: push the new tab and remove the old route a few frames later. It was not done because it changes navigation.

items.rootCause: Same mechanism. Per move: my lock's endless PulseBand was deleted at the move result while my avatar started its reaction layers. The flash was cleared at R+900 ms, exactly when the nod ends and AvatarArt draws its still picture. The bot's 22 dp MiniAvatar was deleted when its lock ended, while its card avatar started a reaction. Game → results: the results replace the game in one commit. A load that came back at once put the results' avatars and icons in the frame that deleted the game's recently moved views (~944 failures, frames of 763/801 ms). Found in this re-check: the round-1 retired MiniAvatar was kept as a flex child of the cell's centred column. When the opponent's digit landed, the hidden 22 dp avatar pushed the digit ~11 dp up and partly out of the cell for 4 s, a visible regression. Also (reviewer issue 3): retired parts were hidden only from a passive effect, so they could show for 0-1 frames. The reviewer was also right that the results' loading state (spinner plus 'טוען את התוצאה…') was visible for 2 frames plus the results' JS render, not just ~22 ms.
items.fix: Round 1 (kept): LOCK_PULSE is a CSS animation. useRetired/RETIRE_MS = 4000 keeps a cleared or replaced flash and the opponent's MiniAvatar mounted (same key, so the same host view), at rest, until Reanimated has released them. The results route resolves its load afterFrames(2). Spinner is CSS. This round: new PartSlot in Cell.tsx, always rendered around each FlashLayer part and each MiniAvatar. It is a plain View with collapsable={false} and pointerEvents='none', filling the cell absolutely and centring its content. When retired, its own static opacity is 0, in the same React commit, so no frame can show a retired part. The effect only stops the animation. Because the slot is out of the flex flow, a retired avatar can no longer push the digit off centre. A live MiniAvatar was the only flex child of an oppLock cell, so its position is identical. Results: ResultsLoading keeps the spinner and text at opacity 0 for RESULTS_QUIET_MS = 300 ms (past the 240 ms screen fade-in), then shows them unchanged in the same place. A normal game → results never flashes the loading state, and a slow load still shows it. Left unchanged and documented in PERF.md: the FlightLayer score chip deleted at R+740 and LockRing/SecondsPill after their 240 ms fade, because no SVG draw was found in those frames.

perf.notes:
How each review issue was handled:
1. Medium (History filter / Leaderboard tab swap): confirmed and fixed with the SWAP_FRAMES gate. Also fixed the History 'נסה שוב' failure → cards swap from issue 4. Covered by tests, PERF.md and device checks 6, 7 and 8.
2. Low (results loading flash): confirmed. Added RESULTS_QUIET_MS = 300, plus a test and a screen-recording pass/fail check. Removed the wrong '~22 ms at <15%' text from PERF.md.
3. Low (hidden from an effect): fixed with PartSlot, which hides in the same commit. While checking it I found a real visible regression from round 1: the retired MiniAvatar stayed in the cell's flex column and pushed the opponent's new digit ~11 dp up for 4 s. Fixed and tested.
4. Low (other pressed-button cases): History retry is fixed. The rest is documented in PERF.md under what still needs the native patch, with estimates: last-page 'עוד' pressed, back from a screen within ~2.5 s of mount, tab-to-tab router.replace (estimated seconds), leaderboard pull-to-refresh with a podium reorder, and a pinned-row variant change. Measurement-only device check 9 covers them.
5. Low (H3): useFocusEffect replaces useEffect. warmModesHit.test proves the markup ModesScreen draws is pre-parsed. Status is now 'expected, pending device numbers'.
6. Low (H2 root cause): refined from code. Home does not re-render on return. react-native-screens sends a ScreenTransitionProgressEvent every frame per screen, and Reanimated re-applies the registry on any UI-thread event. This matches ~30 updates per tag over 150 ms. A device stack trace would confirm it.

Verification, all with --maxWorkers=2, final runs green:
- src/__tests__ (all app-level, including e2e and a11yAudit), board, results, history, leaderboard and home: 112 suites / 2033 tests.
- board, game, levels, replay, dev, and the botPractice, botPracticeEnd and soloPractice e2e: 97 / 1659.
- Earlier broad run over src/components, results, history, leaderboard, home, player, progress, game/online, decimalSites, historyReplay/ranked e2e and startupGraph: 120 / 1710. The one failure was Board.test's /^cell-flash-/ count, fixed by renaming the slot testIDs to cell-slot-*.
- npx tsc -p apps/mobile --noEmit: clean. ESLint: clean on all changed files. prettier --check: clean on all changed files. I ran prettier --write only on my own test files (cellRetire, historySkeletonSwap, leaderboardSwap).

Process notes:
- Shared files were edited with small Edit replacements after re-reading them. One exception: I used a single targeted sed on Cell.tsx and cellRetire.test.tsx to rename the two testID strings I had added this round. Nothing else in those files was touched.
- No locale or UI string changes. No git, APK, adb, deploy, npm install or node_modules changes. The Reanimated native patch was not applied.

Behaviour changes, all intended and small:
- History filter switch: the skeleton shows for at least 2 frames.
- History retry that brings cards: failure → skeleton → cards.
- Leaderboard switch to a cached tab or size: the table skeleton shows for 2 frames plus the rows' JS render. During that time the old rows used to stay. The pinned row and the header update at once.
- Results: the spinner and text appear only after 300 ms.

issues.problem: H1 removes the deleted-while-SVG-draws pattern only for opening History. The same freeze can still happen on History's filter switch and on the Leaderboard tab switch. The fix does not handle this, PERF.md does not mention it, and no device check covers it.
issues.evidence: Reanimated 4.5.1 src/ViewDescriptorsSet.ts add() calls updater(true), and styleUpdater then always calls updateProps when forceUpdate is set. So every useAnimatedStyle view sits in AnimatedPropsRegistry for about 2-2.5 s after it mounts. Every HistoryCard is a PressableCard (tactile.tsx:401, useAnimatedStyle), and the first rows also have an Enter. initialNumToRender=PAGE_SIZE mounts about 20 cards. HistoryScreen.pick() calls setFilter (so shown=null and the skeleton shows) and then run(loader.show(next)). HistoryLoader.show -> fill() does nothing once 'all' has loaded both sources (fillRanked's while loop and fillPractice's early return), so it resolves within microtasks. The skeleton commit and the cards commit therefore reach the UI in one frame. If the switch comes within ~2.5 s of the previous list mounting, the old cards' ~20-26 animated views are deleted in the same frame that draws ~370 new shapes. That is the same order of failures as the original 24x370 freeze. LeaderboardScreen.show() is worse: setTab plus setSnap(feed.peek(...)) swap the old rows for cached rows, with their avatars, in a single commit.
issues.suggestion: Either gate list replacements the way the results are gated (show the new list afterFrames(2) after the old one is gone, or keep the skeleton at least 2 frames after a filter or tab change), or keep the old list mounted, hidden, for RETIRE_MS. At minimum, write this down in PERF.md as remaining for the native patch, and add device checks: History opened, then a filter tapped within 1 s, back and forth; Leaderboard tab A->B->A within 1 s. Each must log 0 'synchronouslyUpdateUIProps failed'.

issues.problem: Results (H4c): the claim that the loading state shows for only ~22 ms at under 15% screen opacity does not account for real timing. The content is committed only after rAF #2 and after the whole JS render of the results screen. Meanwhile the loading state (Spinner plus the 'results.loading' text) is already mounted alone and fading in, so a visible loading flash before the results is likely on the A16.
issues.evidence: app/results/[id].tsx: load = afterFrames(2) then result. ResultsScreen.tsx:162-165 shows the loading state with a Spinner and t('results.loading'). Frame N (game teardown plus the loading mount) is not short on the A16. The results' JS render (avatars, count-ups) runs after rAF #2, while the native fade (160-240 ms, 'Android fades at its own pace', transitions.ts) keeps going. Before the fix, the measured failures show the content landed in the deletion frame, so no loading state was seen.
issues.suggestion: Keep the loading state invisible for the first ~250 ms (for example a CSS fade-in with an animationDelay, or only the background during the frame gate) so it can never flash. Otherwise make 'no visible spinner or loading text between game and results' an explicit pass/fail device check, with a screen recording.

issues.problem: Retired cell parts are hidden from a passive effect (a shared-value set), not in the commit that retires them. For 0-1 UI frames the bot's 22 dp avatar can still show under its just-placed digit, on top of the correct-flash fill. A flash replaced mid-fade can also overlap the new one for a frame. Before, both were deleted in the same commit, so 'visually identical' is not strictly true.
issues.evidence: Cell.tsx MiniAvatar: useEffect(() => { if (retired) { cancelAnimation(scale); seen.set(0); ... } }). FlashLayer has a retire effect with cancelAnimation and opacity.set(0). The React commit (digit plus the kept avatar at opacity 1) mounts on the UI thread before the runOnUI from the effect has run, and the change to 0 lands only in a following Reanimated commit. The cellRetire tests check the state after act() flushes effects, so they cannot see this frame.
issues.suggestion: Hide retired parts in the same React commit while keeping the same animated host view: wrap each retired MiniAvatar or FlashLayer in a plain View whose static style is opacity 0 when retired (not display:none, which Fabric unmounts). Keep the effect only to stop the animation.

issues.problem: The same mechanism (a pressed TactileSurface deleted in the frame that draws new card SVG) remains on History and similar screens beyond H2's back arrow. Not documented.
issues.evidence: History 'נסה שוב' (StateView action Button -> TactileSurface body and face, tactile.tsx:316-317): after a press, if the answer arrives within 2 s, the StateView is replaced by cards with ~370 new shapes, about 2 tags x 370 failures. On the last 'עוד' page, shown.hasMore becomes false, so a footer Button pressed under 2 s earlier is deleted in the commit that mounts 20 new cards. Going back from History within ~2 s of the cards mounting deletes ~20-26 freshly written card views, while H2 reports ~30 Home shapes drawn on every return.
issues.suggestion: List these under 'what still needs the native patch' in PERF.md (B14/B32, הרצת QA 3), or apply afterFrames or retire gating to these swaps too. Add a device check: History offline -> 'נסה שוב' -> back online.

issues.problem: H3 is marked 'fixed' without a measurement on the device, and the test does not prove that ModesScreen hits the warmed caches. The warm-up also does not check focus, so in the first session it can run in the middle of a game.
issues.evidence: warmModes.test.ts compares against its own picture() helper (AVATAR_SIZES[size].image, 'tile', 'neutral'). It never renders ModesScreen and asserts that parse is not called, so a future change to Avatar sizes, crop or expression would silently stop the warming. HomeScreen.tsx:114 runs useEffect(() => splashGone ? warmModesLater(localAvatar) : undefined) with no focus check, and Home stays mounted under the game. If a game starts within 1.2 s, the barrel require plus two svg parses run at a JS idle moment during play.
issues.suggestion: Add a test that calls warmModes(id), then renders ModesScreen and expects svg.parse not to be called. Skip the warm-up when Home is not the focused screen. Report H3 as 'expected, pending device numbers' until framestats confirm ~250-300 ms.

issues.problem: H2 (needs-moshe) has an incomplete root cause: the ~30 Home shapes drawn on every return were not identified. If they come from Home re-mounting icons or avatar parts on focus, removing that redraw would fix H2, and the back-from-History case, without touching the press feel or the native patch.
issues.evidence: The fix result says: 'I did not identify which ~30 Home shapes are drawn on return.' System Back gives 0 failures only because nothing stale is deleted, not because no shapes are drawn.
issues.suggestion: Before asking Moshe to choose the native patch or CSS presses, find which Home shapes get a first draw (setClientRect) on return, for example by logging VirtualView tags in a debug build or diffing Home renders on focus.

review.summary: I checked the changes against the Reanimated 4.5.1 source and the H1/H4 mechanism holds. performNonLayoutOperations (ReanimatedModuleProxy.cpp:815-823) re-applies only animatedPropsRegistry_->getPendingUpdates(). CSS animations live in cssAnimationsRegistry_. ANDROID_SYNCHRONOUSLY_UPDATE_UI_PROPS is false, so CSS updates go through shadow-tree commits, which skip deleted views. AnimatedComponent.componentWillUnmount marks a node removable, and ReanimatedMountHook.handleNodeRemovals drops it after mount; otherwise getSettledUpdates drops it after 2 s. So the CSS Skeleton, Spinner and LOCK_PULSE really leave the registry: History's 24 pulsing blocks can no longer fail on each new shape. The look is preserved: the loop curve [0.42,0,0.58,1] is symmetric, so 'alternate' equals withRepeat reverse, and all three are off under reduced motion. useRetired/RETIRE_MS (4 s, past the 2 s GC plus the 500 ms poll) keeps flashes and the opponent's mini avatar with the same keys, so the same host view stays, and it clears its timers on unmount. Retired parts are pointerEvents none or inside the cell's labelled Pressable, so TalkBack does not read them and they catch no taps. afterFrames(2) for the results fits how Android dispatches frames. Tests: I ran the 7 new or updated suites (38 tests) and 42 related suites (board, results, game, levels, history, leaderboard, startupGraph, homeTransitions); all pass. tsc -p apps/mobile is clean and eslint is clean on the changed files. The new tests would fail on the old code: they assert an empty worklet style plus the CSS config, the same host view after a flash is cleared, and the 2-frame gate. Issues: (1) medium: the same freeze can still happen on History when a filter is switched within ~2.5 s, because loader.show resolves in microtasks and the old PressableCard/Enter views were written on mount (updater(true)). The Leaderboard tab switch (feed.peek) is the same. Neither is fixed, documented, or in a device check. (2) The results loading state is likely visible longer than the claimed ~22 ms at under 15%. (3) Retired parts are hidden from an effect, so the mini avatar can show for 0-1 frames. (4) Retry, last-page 'עוד' and back-from-History have the same pressed-button deletion. (5) H3 is reported fixed without device numbers, the test does not prove that ModesScreen hits the cache, and the warm-up can run during a game. (6) H2's Home redraw on return is not identified. Files reviewed: C:/Users/mosheg/Documents/ReactNative/sudoku-fight/apps/mobile/src/components/ui/{Skeleton,Spinner}.tsx, cssMotion.ts and retire.ts; C:/Users/mosheg/Documents/ReactNative/sudoku-fight/apps/mobile/src/components/board/Cell.tsx; C:/Users/mosheg/Documents/ReactNative/sudoku-fight/apps/mobile/app/results/[id].tsx; C:/Users/mosheg/Documents/ReactNative/sudoku-fight/apps/mobile/src/screens/home/{warmModes.ts,HomeScreen.tsx}; C:/Users/mosheg/Documents/ReactNative/sudoku-fight/apps/mobile/src/screens/history/{HistoryScreen.tsx,historyLoader.ts}; C:/Users/mosheg/Documents/ReactNative/sudoku-fight/apps/mobile/src/screens/leaderboard/LeaderboardScreen.tsx; C:/Users/mosheg/Documents/ReactNative/sudoku-fight/docs/PERF.md.

items.rootCause: The rule that decided whether to show my name was a fixed threshold, not the name's real width. In ModesScreen.tsx Me, the name showed when Me's laid-out width was at least ME_NAME_ROOM = avatar 34 + gap 8 + 24 = 66 dp. The intent was 'room for a few letters ("Mos…")', so the old test even expected a cut name. On a 360x780 dp phone, 'Новая партия' and 'Nueva partida' leave Me roughly 66–82 dp. That passes the 66 threshold, but 'אחוותא' needs 40 + 8 + 34 = 82 dp (Rubik 500 13, measured), so the name was squeezed to 'אחוו…'. de/th/ja titles are short (Me > 82, so the name is whole). fr/id titles are long (Me < 66, so the name is hidden). Only languages whose leftover falls between the two numbers showed the bug.
items.fix:
ModesScreen.tsx (Me): the decision now uses two widths the phone lays out:
- Me's own width (onLayout);
- the name's own width, from a new MeasureName: the same isolated name, same style, in an absolute, opacity-0, pointerEvents none, accessibility-hidden box as wide as the window, at Me's start, where nothing squeezes it.
New pure meShowsName(room, nameWidth): nameWidth + space[4] + avatar.compact.frame <= room.
The name is either whole or not rendered. While either width is unknown it renders at opacity 0 (no one-frame '…' flash). Me stays one accessible element labelled with the name, and its width does not depend on content (flexBasis 0), so nothing oscillates.
The measured width is tied to the name it was measured for, and MeasureName is keyed by the name: a renamed profile is re-measured even when it is the same width.
ME_NAME_ROOM was removed. components.md §19.1 now says 'shows only where all of it fits, by the widths the phone laid out, never cut with "…"'.

items.rootCause:
All four were one-line texts (numberOfLines 1) in a fixed room, so a longer text could only end in '…':
- Home rating chip: Rating's stacked chip (Rubik 500 11) in its column, 90 dp wide less padding and border = 76 dp text room.
- New Game section note: SectionLabel note in the 286 dp section row, with a flex rule that could also shrink to 0. That is why the ranked line showed no rule at all in en-XA.
- New Game tagline: ModeCard tagline in the 214 dp text column.
- Settings testing row: RowButton title, 224 dp room in Settings.
Real languages are held to one line by existing tests (HomeAccount, modesFit, ModesAndGameType), so only en-XA (~+40%) overflowed. Any longer future translation would have been cut the same way.

items.rootCause: StarsBar draws each number under the bar (Teko 600 15) absolutely, at start = tick% with a fixed translateX of -6 dp. Its width was never measured, and it had no font-scale cap. At scale 1.0, on the A16's 352 dp bar, '15.5' spans 297–318 and '17.5' spans 336–356 (4 dp past the bar end, inside the gutter). At ×2.0 both double: '15.5' (42 dp) runs into '17.5' ('15.517.5'), and '17.5' runs about 30 dp past the bar, beyond the 16 dp gutter, so its last digit is cut at the screen edge. The numbers row was a fixed 17 dp, so large digits also hung below it. Every bar shares this code. For example, a time bar's last number sits at 100% ('60' at W−6).
items.fix:
StarsBar.tsx, a new Numbers part:
- The numbers are HUD text: Text scale 'hud', capped at ×1.35 like the rest of the level HUD (BRD-3). Their row height is numbersHeight(scale, lines): 17 at 1.0, 22 at the cap.
- Placement uses measured widths: onLayout of the row (axis width) and of each number (keyed by its mark and text).
- New pure placeNumbers(shares, widths, axis, scale): each number keeps its designed place (6 before its tick) unless that runs it within 4 dp of the next, or past the axis end further than it hangs at design size (width/scale). Then it moves just enough: a right-to-left pass, then a left-to-right pass.
- If one line can't hold them, every other number from the last goes on a second line.
- The axis is direction 'ltr', so this is the same in RTL and LTR. Until widths are known it draws as before (translateX -6). At 1.0 the result equals the old positions, so the visible design is unchanged.
- components.md §19.5 is updated.
For L041 at ×2.0 (capped to ×1.35): '13' at 248–263, '15.5' at 297–325, '17.5' moves 7 dp left to 329–356 (no further right than at 1.0). They are 4 dp apart, and each still sits over its tick.
items.test:
StarsBar.test.tsx, new describe with real Teko widths (widthIn):
- At 1.0 placeNumbers equals tick−6 for '13/15.5/17.5' on a 352 axis, and '17.5' hangs past the end as designed.
- At ×1.35 and ×2: the old placement hung further than designed (and collided at ×2); the new one is apart, no end beyond the design end, no start < 0, and each covers its tick.
- A time bar (40/50/60 of 60 s) at 1.0 and the cap: apart, no further than designed.
- The stagger case is on 2 lines and apart.
- A rendered hunter bar at window fontScale 2: maxFontSizeMultiplier 1.35, the row height is numbersHeight(1.35) > 17, the design translateX of -6 before layout, and after the layout events the translateX values match placeNumbers and are apart.
It fails on the old code (no placeNumbers/numbersHeight, no cap). The level HUD tests (ideas, levelHuds, levelStage) pass.
